headline: Japanese 101 Master 20
threshold: Practice everyday Japanese with English support; lesson completion is not a proficiency credential.

lessons.title: Introduce a classmate to the study group
lessons.objective: Introduce a classmate to the study group: Introduce a new group member, ask about a preference, recall a meeting with polite past ～ました, make a plan with ～つもりです, and describe how studying went with an い-adjective past (たのしい → たのしかったです).
lessons.focus: Introduce a new group member, ask about a preference, recall a meeting with polite past ～ました, make a plan with ～つもりです, and describe how studying went with an い-adjective past (たのしい → たのしかったです).

words.en: Aki, what kind of books do you like?

lessons.title: Pack for the first class
lessons.objective: Pack for the first class: Read a supplies note, count items, and clarify which things are needed. Bound notebooks use ～さつ: にさつ means two notebooks. The polite request is ～てください: もつ becomes もって, くる becomes きて, so もってきてください means “please bring.”

lessons.title: Identity, condition, and location
lessons.objective: Identity, condition, and location: Separate who someone is, how they feel, and where they are. つかれています describes a resulting state (“is tired”), not an action in progress.

lessons.title: Clarify the route to a meeting

lessons.title: Explain how you study a difficult word
lessons.objective: Explain how you study a difficult word: Ask どうやって ('how') and explain a repeatable study strategy rather than only listing a daily schedule. Use ききます for asking a teacher, やりかた for a method, and すこしずつ for gradual progress. Reuse polite question-and-answer turns.

lessons.title: Reply to a short message
lessons.objective: Reply to a short message: Read a plan, reply with a time and place, and confirm the meeting. In a written reply, put the exact words inside 「」 and add と after the closing quote: 「…」と かきました / かえしました means “wrote … / replied ….”

lessons.title: Order for two people
lessons.objective: Order for two people: Ask preferences, order for two, and confirm an ingredient that someone does not want. For an ingredient in a dish, はいる becomes はいって. はいっています means “is in it / contains” (a present state), and the negative はいっていません means “is not in it / does not contain it.” This is a present state, not a past event.

あきさんに みせても いいですか。
words.en: May I show it to Aki?

words.es: あきさんの ほんも ここに あります。

lessons.title: Tell yesterday's outing
lessons.objective: Tell yesterday's outing: Narrate several completed actions in polite past, then check one detail with a partner.
lessons.focus: Narrate several completed actions in polite past, then check one detail with a partner.

words.es: きのう ともだちと きょうとへ いきました。
words.en: Yesterday I went to Kyoto with a friend.

words.es: あさ はやく えきに いきました。
words.en: We went to the station early in the morning.

words.es: でんしゃで まちへ いきました。
words.en: We went into town by train.

words.es: ひるごはんを たべました。
そのあと ほんやに いきました。
words.en: After that we went to a bookshop.

words.es: あたらしい ほんを かいました。

lessons.title: A habit versus one event
lessons.objective: A habit versus one event: Contrast what often happened with one dated event; use time words rather than inventing an imperfect tense.
lessons.focus: Contrast what often happened with one dated event; use time words rather than inventing an imperfect tense.

words.es: むかし、まいにち がっこうまで あるきました。
words.en: In the past, I walked to school every day.

words.es: いつも ともだちと いっしょに あるきました。
words.en: I always walked with a friend.

words.es: でも、きのうは でんしゃで いきました。
words.en: But yesterday I went by train.

words.es: あめが ふっていましたから。
えきで ともだちを まちました。
words.en: I waited for my friend at the station.

words.es: それから いっしょに いきました。

lessons.title: A full everyday conversation
lessons.objective: A full everyday conversation: Greet, clarify a word, plan a meeting, refer back to a previous visit, and close a short conversation politely. いってください can mean “please say” (言って) here; the same kana means “please go” (行って) in Master 15. Context identifies the verb.
lessons.focus: Greet, clarify a word, plan a meeting, refer back to a previous visit, and close a short conversation politely. いってください can mean “please say” (言って) here; the same kana means “please go” (行って) in Master 15. Context identifies the verb.

words.es: ありがとうございます
こんにちは。しつもんが あります。
はい、どんな しつもんですか。
この ことばを ゆっくり いってください。
はい、「しりょう」です。わかりますか。
words.en: Yes, it is “shiryō” (materials or a handout). Do you understand?

words.es: はい、ありがとうございます。あした どこで あいますか。
words.en: Yes, thank you. Where shall we meet tomorrow?
